name: Liutciia Berkutova
title: Liutciia Berkutova: The Flight She Did Not Board
dek: Stranded in Saudi Arabia, she let the evacuation flight leave and built a business. Eighteen years on, the girl from Izhevsk runs WorldZen, a company without borders.
excerpt: Liutciia Berkutova was born in Izhevsk in 1990 and built a desert aviation business while stranded in Saudi Arabia. Now she helps others cross borders with WorldZen.
seoDescription: Liutciia Berkutova, founder of WorldZen, on Izhevsk, GulfDzen, starting again and building a visa and relocation company without borders.
content:
In July 2020 the Russian Embassy announced an evacuation flight out of Saudi Arabia. Liutciia Berkutova had a way home, and the temporary support she had received could not continue indefinitely. She did not board. She stayed at her own risk and kept building a business that had started with one Instagram story.

That decision sits at the centre of a life she describes as eighteen years of reinvention. She was born in 1990 in Izhevsk, the capital of Udmurtia, a year before the Soviet Union ceased to exist. The city is known as Russia's arms capital and still has no major international airport. She did not grow up with influential connections or an inherited business. What she had was curiosity. Her surname comes from berkut, the Russian name for the golden eagle.

From the desk to the desert

Her first work in tourism began in 2008, while she was studying: package holidays, booking systems, international passports for her family, and in time her sister's wedding in Sri Lanka. After university she worked for a year as an economist, including work on tenders. Ten hours a day at a computer made her question it. In 2015 she moved to Phuket to work with Coral Travel, then to Cyprus, where she trained as a croupier and spent about a year and a half in a casino.

In 2019 Saudi Arabia opened to international tourism, and she went to see it. She worked on projects connected with Riyadh Season and Winter at Tantora in AlUla. Then the pandemic closed the borders. The embassy helped her with accommodation and food, and she assisted with documents and visa applications for people pursuing education or business in the Kingdom.

A local pilot she met through Couchsurfing invited her up in a small recreational aircraft. She filmed it, posted it, and people asked where they could book. Twenty came to the first gathering. That was the beginning of GulfDzen, which added desert picnics, live cooking, barbecues, parties and group transport, and later aviation experiences around Dammam and the Arabian Gulf. Within roughly a year she had earned enough to buy an apartment.

Starting again

February 2022 brought serious investment losses. Her long absence from Saudi Arabia had also exposed the business to problems of trust and financial misconduct within the team, and she stopped operating GulfDzen. She became a freelancer and content creator, working on exhibitions, conferences and events in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. In October 2024 she returned to Saudi Arabia on a business visa to work at the opening of Sindalah, NEOM's luxury island destination.

The years since have moved quickly. In 2026 she marked five years of life in the Emirates. She turned down a marriage proposal whose expectations did not align with her values. In February she flew to South Africa, learned to surf and completed her first bungee jump. On June 12, Russia Day and the anniversary of the founding of Izhevsk, she reached Makkah.

A company without borders

That path became WorldZen, which helps people with visas, relocation and international travel. Some clients need a holiday. Others want to move for work, establish residency or discover Russia. She registered the business in Russky Vozhoy, the Udmurt village she moved to after returning from Saudi Arabia, because she wanted to build an international company from where her story began. She is also developing a broader vision for a digital platform to help people understand mobility pathways and organize documentation.

Her plans reach further: a foundation for women who have survived abuse, a mosque in the Middle East, an airline called BerkutZen with routes from Izhevsk, and the WorldZen mobile visa and relocation application. She is clear that she is not starting over. In her words, she is beginning with eighteen years of experience.
